title: How Sink Drainage Works: Understanding Traps and Vents
description: A properly functioning sink drainage system relies on a careful balance of gravity, water seals, and atmospheric pressure. The P-trap beneath the sink holds a standing column of water that prevents sewer gases from entering the living space, while the vent system allows air to enter behind the flowing water, preventing siphoning and ensuring smooth, rapid drainage. Without adequate venting, water can gurgle or drain sluggishly as pressure vacuums pull water out of the trap seal. Knowing how these components interact helps plumbers diagnose drainage issues accurately and ensure installations comply with venting principles.
